title: A finite sum with one omitted term
statement: Let $m$ be a natural number, let $j\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$, and let $q$ be a nonnegative extended real number. The sum over all $a\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$ that contributes $0$ at $a=j$ and $q$ otherwise is $(m-1)q$, where the right-hand side means the sum of $m-1$ copies of $q$.
hypotheses_covered: $q$ is a nonnegative extended real number
